newsitem.title: JAPAN: Natural to feel dlr/yen rate at 'good' level -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Natural to feel dlr/yen rate at 'good' level -- MOF.

text.p: It is natural to feel that the dollar/yen exchange rate has come to a "good" level, Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa told a news conference on Monday.

Asked whether Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's comments earlier in the day that currencies should stabilise soon meant that the ministry thought that the yen's strengthening was too rapid, Ogawa said: "It is natural to think that if such a level continues it has come to a good place."
He added that the message from the Group of Seven (G7) nations' agreement on foreign exchange at their meeting in late April had "rather rapidly" filtered through to the markets.
Ogawa said recent currency moves are unlikely to affect Japan's economy substantially.
"When we consider currency levels at which Japanese firms had planned their business activities, I don't think current (currency) moves will considerably affect their economic activities," he said.
Ogawa added that the firmness of Japan's economy is unlikely to be undermined by the rise of the yen.
